title: Liverpool Unlocked
blurb: A digital twin of Liverpool and Birkenhead, turned into a Roblox game with my kids.
html:
A family project. My kids and I took a digital twin of Liverpool and Birkenhead and turned it into a Roblox game, so you can explore the city we live in, from the Three Graces and the Royal Albert Dock to Mathew Street and Hamilton Square.

You can drive around town, pick up passengers as a taxi driver, ride the scooters, the bus, the big wheel and the Mersey ferry, or get catapulted across the river, as in the trailer. There are challenges too: cooking, delivery driving, rescue missions, and chasing down a seagull that has nicked your chips. Along the way you pick up a bit of local history, take selfies with the Mersey Moptops and earn Mersey points for the leaderboard.

The same kind of city model I use for digital twins at work, just with a lot more seagulls. Have you got what it takes to become a true Scouser?

title: Liverpool City Region Digital Twin
blurb: A digital twin of the whole Liverpool City Region in Unreal Engine, with live business intelligence from Soundings.
html:
A digital twin of the whole Liverpool City Region, built in Unreal Engine, with realtime business data intelligence from Soundings brought in on top.

The demo flies from Southport to Daresbury and from Birkenhead across the Mersey to St Helens, stopping at each cluster to show the creative and digital companies around it: the waterfront and commercial quarter, the Knowledge Quarter, Ten Streets, the Baltic Triangle, Knowsley Business Park, Prescot and more. Every count and label comes from the live data rather than a slide, so the picture stays as current as Soundings does.

It's an early look at where I'd like digital twins to go: a place you can fly around and ask questions of, where the answer is a query rather than a commissioned report.

title: VP Futures
blurb: An intensive six-week training scheme with Industrial Light & Magic, Epic Games and the National Film and Television School
html:
Earlier this year I spent 6 weeks on an intensive training course with Epic Games, Industrial Light and Magic, the National Film and Television School and Future Screens Belfast to learn the art of Virtual Production.

Got to work on a number of stages, learning everything about the process from some of the top names and pioneers in the industry.

The course and masterclasses covered:

  • Technical set-ups for nDisplay, tracking systems, colour management (OCIO), ICVFX, multi-user servers and source control
  • Content creation, including environment building, technical art, VFX, optimisation, pre-visualisation, location scouting and even some sessions on motion capture
  • Stage operations, tech art and optimisation

Got to meet some epic names and world-class pioneers in the space from ILM and more. And spent time working on volumes at the Epic Innovation Centre in London and Studio Ulster in Belfast.

Mind blown. Have since been up to some things in a few other stages bringing my Unreal Engine knowledge into film and TV production. Exciting times.

For a great behind-the-scenes look at this pioneering programme, check out StoryFutures.

title: Annwn: Transmission 000
blurb: A trailer for Annwn, a story of the Welsh Otherworld, and an experiment in consistent AI animation built in ComfyUI.
html:
Annwn is the Otherworld of Welsh myth, the realm that runs through the Mabinogion. Transmission 000 is a trailer for a story set on its edges: a girl living in a pink caravan deep in a Welsh forest, a book of old stories, a television showing something it shouldn't, and a doorway in the trees.

It was also an experiment, in late 2024, with the hardest problem in AI animation: keeping a character the same from one shot to the next. I built the pipeline in ComfyUI.

  • Character LoRAs. I trained LoRAs on the main characters so they keep their faces, hair, clothes and proportions through very different shots, lighting and angles.
  • Multi-angle 3D views. From a single character design I generated consistent turnarounds and multi-angle views, used as training data for the LoRAs and as reference for posing and framing each shot.
  • Bespoke nodes. I wrote custom ComfyUI nodes to fill the gaps in the off-the-shelf tools, carrying character references, style and shot set-ups through the graph so every scene starts from the same place.
  • Keyframes to motion. Consistent keyframes were animated with image-to-video models, then upscaled and graded so the shots cut together as one film.

The soundtrack is by MOEA, my music R&D project. It follows on from my earlier experiments with creatures from Annwn.

title: Mathew Street in Blender
blurb: A digital twin of Mathew Street, home of the Cavern Club, built in Blender and lit for day and night.
html:
A digital twin experiment on one of Liverpool's most famous streets. Mathew Street is home to the Cavern Club, and it is a narrow canyon of pubs, bars and shopfronts that you really need 3D to capture.

It is built in Blender from the street plan up: building footprints and roofs first, then facades, windows and shopfronts, then the details that make it Mathew Street, from the tables outside The Grapes to the Cavern Pub sign and the Cavern Wall of Fame, its bricks carrying the names of the acts who played there. The same scene is lit twice, once in daylight and once at night with the lamps and neon on.

A companion to the Liverpool waterfront in Blender, and part of my wider digital twin work in the city.

title: Liverpool Waterfront in Blender
blurb: A digital twin experiment rebuilding Liverpool's waterfront in Blender, from city-block massing to the Three Graces on the Mersey.
html:
A digital twin experiment, this time in Blender. It starts from a simple massing model of the city centre, plain blocks laid out on the street plan, and works up from there.

The Royal Liver Building is built up in place from a reference photo, clock towers, Liver Birds and all. Then the scene is lit and rendered as a view across the Mersey: the Three Graces on the Pier Head, with a ferry at the landing stage.

It sits alongside my other digital twin work, including the city region twin in Unreal Engine and Liverpool Unlocked in Roblox: the same city, built different ways for different jobs.

html:
Been working on a number of projects and advising several businesses around AI conversational agents, and their use cases, everything from customer service to education and health.

Working on ways to control and contain information so we can have some AI buddies to help us with our lives.

Get in touch to find out more.

title: Pinky in Blender
blurb: GPT-6 Astra and Blender MCP model, rig and animate my daughter's fluffy pink octopus.
html:
Another GPT-6 Astra and Blender experiment. This time the brief was to model, rig and animate my daughter's character, Pinky Pop, the pink fluffy octopus.

The agent works inside Blender through Blender MCP. A few hours and some tweaks later, it had built the octopus, rigged all eight arms, animated the mouth, eyes and gaze, relit the scene, and rendered a couple of sequences.

It is very rough around the edges and far from perfect, and there is still plenty that needs the human touch. But in the hands of a skilled modeller and animator, I think this kind of workflow, with AI as a collaborator, could get really interesting. As a nice side effect, it also ended up teaching my daughter a thing or two about Blender and 3D along the way.

The video is the Blender behind the scenes and the direct output, with no extra AI or video-to-video passes on the renders at the end.

title: MOEA
blurb: An art experiment with song composition, sound and moving image, with two demo albums out so far.
html:
MOEA is an art experiment with song composition, sound and moving image.

All original compositions from over the years, and some from my younger, angrier & grungier band days, but re-imagined.

I'm planning on working with MOEA as a bit of a creative and innovation outlet for learning/testing new processes around sound synthesis, ethical and human-centred approaches to new production tools, assistive AI as well as hands on research with distribution, marketing, live experiences, fan engagement and more.

First demo album released in March 2025 is called Alpha. It's very early stage, raw and embryonic and totally unfinished ;) I probably shouldn't have, but I released it anyway as part of the process so people can see the evolution.

The second demo album is a lot more experimental and surreal, called Dream Machine, it came out in May 2025 and is all instrumentals - follow us on MOEA Spotify for updated tracks as they drop.

I'm working on the next set of tracks in late 2025, which are mainly instrumentals and based on the songs in 'Alpha'... plus a few more ideas I've been toying with.

MOEA is distributed and published with Ditto Music and Sentric Publishing, some of our partners in MusicFutures.

You can subscribe to the progress and see some of the experimental videos and tracks on:

MOEA Spotify

MOEA YouTube

MOEA TikTok

MOEA Instagram

Press Articles and Reviews:

MOEA Illustrate Magazine Review

MOEA Avanzada Magazine Review

MOEA AcidTest Review

MOEA Last Day Dead Review

Processes and Disclosures

So I am not using generative AI tools for the compositions/songwriting as that's my thing... This is a creative outlet for my work.

But I am using Assistive AI quite a bit in various aspects of realising the work and supporting the project:

  • My songwriting process always starts with a guitar or a keyboard. I spend a lot of time looping with pedals in my home studio to get the ideas down... then using that as the base for the creative process. It's how I figure things out, sometimes over many months, years and even decades. It's my slow thing and I don't mind taking time on this.
  • The voice on the first album originated with my terrible voice transformed into MIDI, then using a paid and licensed trained singer to help realise it with midi to voice synthesis (and get it in tune!).
  • It started as a test but I felt quite uncomfortable with this to be honest... hence evolving into instrumentals after the first release. I need to learn to sing but I have a terrible timbre (I wasn't the singer back in my band days). It was sort of an experiment to see how real I could get it sounding. I'm sorry if it offended, but I can assure you everyone was paid for their work here.
  • I'm updating Alpha to reflect this change of direction! Although I find, as mainly a composer, this process is very helpful in terms of getting down and noodling with base ideas. This has been really transformative for me in the ideation and creative process of bringing a vision to life.
  • I am using similar process to this occasionally to create melody lines, i.e. humming melody lines into a computer to get the midi notes to convert into instrumentation. Although I mainly do this on my guitar and other instruments, I can see this being really helpful for a lot of people. Especially as I'm mainly a writer, not a performer these days.
  • I am using AI Mastering Tools and some assistive features in Logic Pro, which is my main DAW. Using a number of plugins (e.g. Native Instruments magic for the synth, arpeggiators and instrumentals). Some synth based instruments are getting really good now, and am finding myself mixing them in a lot more these days to augment my analogue origins.
  • The Video and Marketing of MOEA make extensive use of Assistive AI and Generative AI (it's pretty obvious and I always disclose on social) including help with Press Releases, Album Art and Music Videos. Visual AI is a big part of my R&D for my job too, and how I make my living as a technologist/developer... so I need to be on top of this for my future career.
  • These tools include custom ComfyUI and VFX workflows (made by me), Midjourney, Runway, Kling, ChatGPT, Google Veo, Unreal Engine, After Effects and some custom tools and workflows I have built myself (e.g. with Python)
  • I often start with original images/sketches or input video/3D and imagery and get the machines to help with the realisations of the ideas for the videos- lots of the characters are from my two children's imagination. There is a LOT of human process, imagination and decision making in the way I work here.
  • We're always happy to use AI/Tech to take someone else's job, just not our own! I think artists really need to think about this when using AI too.
  • Some of the song titles come out of extensive discussions with chatbots and I often ask them for help with music theory (and getting interesting keys/scales to work with). I am not a formally trained musician so this is useful.
  • I post a lot of my processes on LinkedIn and social media, always disclosing the tools that I use and aim to be transparent and as ethical as possible in this work. As an advocate for certain uses of AI, I think it is important that more people are transparent about what they are doing. I know disclosure is probably challenging for a lot of people, as they don't want to be associated with the existential threat of AI, but given evidence that many/most artists/studios are now using AI in some way, I think it's important to do this.
  • Without some of these tools, I just wouldn't have been able to realise this project. I would always totally prefer to pay humans though, but it is just a side project at the moment and other parts of my life are getting expensive. This is the incredible thing about AI for me... and I hope in some way it can be democratising to other people who just don't get a chance.
  • I'm not doing this to be popular or to make any money (damn music industry!), for me I want to keep this as a fun creative and experimental thing. If that was the purpose I would have probably picked a more generic and bland genre... my music is pretty niche, often messy and sometimes a bit odd. My aim is to be myself here. I am donating all of my royalties from this to charity.
  • Been working on this since late 2024 as MOEA. But many of the songs originate from much earlier when I first learned to play the guitar and start writing over 30 years ago (I have the tapes and CDs from over 20 years ago). I was in a few bands back in my teens and twenties, but life took over, we moved away from each other and got boring jobs and families.
  • Always happy to share more about my processes, please get in touch if you would like to find out more.
  • I recognise that as a human, I am also trained on the world around me: creativity never happens in a bubble, and I owe a lot to my musical and artistic influences, life experiences and my being a sensing soul in the world... I can't trace it all, but lots of this is in the songs hopefully. Humans borrow and steal things too, we build on, adapt and transform all that has gone before: this isn't just an AI challenge.
  • I feel that artists like me (who are using AI in assistive ways, or for marketing, mastering, or just to realise and experiment with ideas with little money or time etc) probably make up quite a bit of the indie scene right now, evidence suggests it's around 30-60% of indie artists using AI in these ways and much more if you include other altering tools, and we shouldn't be put into the same box as the fake Suno/Udio bands. But maybe we all need to be a bit more honest with this, as there has always been a lot of deception in this industry.
  • We need to move away from the dichotomies being created now. AI isn't bad/good. It can be an incredibly collaborative part of the process of realising a vision, but it should ultimately, still be a tool for humans.
  • I hope that you can still hear the human expression and authenticity in the songs. I hope that one day I can afford to do this properly, but until then, this is how I am going to make my music work for me and I hope that it helps others get their voices heard too.
  • Thanks for reading and listening.

title: Air Instrument
blurb: Playing drums and synth in thin air, with a webcam and MediaPipe hand tracking.
html:
No keys, no pads, no controller. Just a webcam, two hands and MediaPipe hand tracking, turning gestures into music in real time.

Each hand has a job. The left one is the drummer: raise and drop fingers to bring the kick, snare, hi-hat and clap in and out of the beat. The right one is the synth: move it to shift the pitch and pinch to ride the volume. A waveform stretches between your hands and wobbles with whatever you're playing, and a step sequencer ticks along underneath.

A quick experiment from June 2025, while I was playing around with sound and new ways of making it. Think of it as a theremin that comes with its own drummer. It is surprisingly hard to stop once you start.

title: If these walls could talk...
blurb: World's first UNESCO Mixed Reality/Hololens/Quest & Integrated Immersive Projection Experience.
html:
“If these walls could talk…” is a collaboration with the Centre for Architecture and the Visual Arts (CAVA) at University of Liverpool, Culture Liverpool, Microsoft, Dimension Studios, Immersive Storylab and Draw and Code.

I am creating an interactive mixed reality Hololens prototype that will take place in the old 19th Century jail cells in the iconic UNESCO World Heritage building St George's Hall, allowing people to interact with the past.

Using cutting edge holographic capture technology to create interactive performances with characters from the past, this experience will enable visitors to go back in time, to really feel what it was like in a 19th Century prison and justice system.

Exciting.

title: Podcast Machine & Digital Double
blurb: From a topic to a talking digital human: an automated podcast pipeline into NVIDIA Omniverse and Unreal Engine.
html:
Type in a topic, press a button, and a digital human starts presenting a podcast about it.

The Dreamlab Podcast Machine was a prototype from early 2024 that chained the whole thing together. A large language model writes the podcast script, ElevenLabs gives it a voice, and the audio goes into NVIDIA Omniverse Audio2Face, which generates the lip sync and facial animation in real time. That drives a digital character in Unreal Engine, so the topic comes out the other end as a performance rather than a text file.

A quick, scrappy build, filmed on my phone off the monitors, so forgive the wobble. It was a useful way to find the joins between the tools, and an early look at how automated content and digital doubles might fit together.

title: Take On Me Portal
seoTitle: Take On Me Portal: Mixed Reality on Quest
blurb: Walking through a portal into a pencil-sketch world on Oculus Quest, after the famous Take On Me music video.
html:
The 1985 video for a-ha's Take On Me is still one of the great bits of mixed media: a pencil-sketch world, a character who reaches out of a comic, and a real person pulled through the page. I wanted to recreate the technical approach behind it and find out what that idea feels like when you can walk into it yourself.

On an Oculus Quest with passthrough on, a portal opens in a real doorway at home. On the other side is a hand-drawn world, all ink lines and cross-hatching, generated as a 360° environment with Blockade Labs' Skybox AI, with a character living in it. Step through and you are inside the sketch. Turn round and the real world is still there through the doorway, in full colour, carrying on without you.

An early 2023 experiment with augmented reality portals. The trick is the same one at the heart of the original video: two worlds, one drawn and one real, with a doorway between them.

title: Pinky Pop in Candyland
blurb: AI 3D animation with my daughter, working out the workflows to bring her character to life.
html:
Pinky Pop is my daughter's character: a fuzzy pink octopus with enormous eyes and a very serious sweet tooth. In 2025 the two of us set out to bring her to life with AI 3D animation, and this little film is where we got to.

Pinky climbs a tower of cookies, slides down hills of sugar, finds a giant gem in a crystal cave, hides behind a lollipop, meets a shark in a sweetie reef, builds a sandcastle out of sprinkles and watches the sun go down from a cliff of chocolate cake. Candyland, in other words.

Most of the work was in the workflow: keeping Pinky looking like Pinky from shot to shot, getting the fuzzy texture and the expressions right, and building a world around her that felt like hers. She was the creative director and I was the tech support, which is the best kind of R&D.

In 2026 Pinky came back as a proper 3D character, modelled, rigged and animated in Blender by GPT-6 Astra.

title: Camera Control in ComfyUI
blurb: One still, any camera angle: a ComfyUI workflow that re-shoots an AI scene from new viewpoints while keeping the character consistent.
html:
One of the trickiest parts of AI filmmaking is coverage. You get a shot you love, and then you need the close-up, the reverse and the low angle, of the same character in the same place.

This ComfyUI workflow treats a single image like a set you can walk a camera around. It takes one frame of a girl outside her caravan in the forest and re-shoots it: an extreme close-up on her face, a low angle looking up, a high angle looking down, a view from behind, a wider shot. A camera control prompt generator turns the move you want into instructions, and an image-editing model with a camera-angle LoRA renders the new view while keeping her, her clothes and the world consistent.

Part of the same work on consistent characters as Annwn: Transmission 000: giving an AI film real coverage to cut between.

title: AI Animation
blurb: Work on techniques, workflows and tooling for AI Animation
html:
As you might know, I've got a super interest in stories of the landscape, lots of my own work is about bringing together technology and place.

And in particular am getting really fascinated with Welsh folklore at the moment with the kids.

Been researching Annwn, the Welsh Otherworld, and stories from the Mabinogion... which was one of the first prose texts compiled in the 13th century... and probably the source of a lot of magic we see in popular culture/Hollywood today. It's so fascinating.

So here's a little experiment with interpreting creatures from Annwn, entirely made using text to video and control tools in AI.

It was included as part of the UKII Intelligence Report 2024 (a report commissioned by Verizon) showcasing 500 trailblazers across industries in the UK.

title: Geospatial Data
blurb: Working with Google Maps inside Unreal Engine, for realtime built environment applications.
html:
A little test with Google Maps inside Unreal Engine, which adds the ability to use data from the whole world inside of games, experiences and realtime tools.

Really excited about the potential of this for work in the built environment (i.e. when combined with other realtime data), and the ways it can enable advanced location scouting and knowledge of the world for production reasons.

Get in touch to find out more.

title: Wonderbeam
blurb: Inventing and developing a shared augmented reality device
html:
We wanted to imagine a more shared way of viewing augmented reality worlds...

Introducing the Wonderbeam.

A social augmented reality device, that lets you share your #ar and #mixedreality worlds with your friends, family, colleagues and connections.

Just imagine playing Ghostbusters with friends in the streets of New York City or discovering the magic of a museum through a new way of engaging with content as you move through space.

Imagine showing architectural/BIM plans on a construction project in progress or improving work productivity with the assistance of digital visual and sonic content.

Imagine learning and spending time with children in a magical new spatial way and new forms of active home and location based entertainment...

We think Wonderbeam has a load of practical and magical possibilities for the world.

6 degrees of freedom, spatially aware, interactive controls, interactive feedback. All working in a little portable projection device that understands its surroundings. Even better with 5G too.

Developed with Dr Mark Wright, Dr Robert Black and my 4 year old boy. Characters in the demo created by Rich Webber.

If you are interested in getting involved in this project, want to bring it to your immersive experience or brand activation, or helping us to raise investment to bring it to mass market, please feel free to contact me on LinkedIn.

title: Infinite Storybook
blurb: An AI picture book that writes and illustrates itself around a child's imagination, with three choices at the end of every page.
html:
Infinite Storybook turns anyone's imagination into an illustrated, interactive picture book in seconds. You mix the ingredients (an age range, a genre and three prompts: a character, a place and a surprise), design the hero, and Google Gemini writes the first page and paints the first illustration.

Then the reader takes over. Every page ends with three choices, like singing along with the frogs in the valley or flying home to tell the other dragons, and each one sends the story somewhere new. The hero stays visually consistent from page to page, the language scales from toddler-simple to pre-teen, and every finished book is saved to a library with its own AI-painted cover, to re-read or carry on later.

For younger children it is a shared adventure with a grown-up; older ones can run the whole thing themselves. It runs in the browser with no account, the stories stay on your own device, and the code is open source.

title: Fantasia Express
blurb: Pioneering Augmented Reality Storytelling on Trains and the transport sector.
html:
Fantasia Express was a 12 month research and development project, awarded by Innovate UK, to Meyouandus and supported by London North Eastern Railway.

I collaborated with the company through Immersive Storylab, alongside AR specialists Corporation Pop, on a project that looked at placing augmented content within and outside a moving rail carriage between London and Edinburgh.

By focusing on AR delivered through the lens of an individual’s mobile device, this project asked questions about how future mixed reality experiences may be embedded within moving vehicles. The project revealed new story worlds in transport, to encourage exploration of place and to act as an exemplar for the possibilities of mixed reality experiences on public and private transport in the future.

My work involved developing the storyworld, characters, narrative dynamics and gameplay for the experience that takes you into a world of imagination and wonder.

title: Dream Machine: Speak a World
blurb: Say what world you want and walk into it: voice-driven AI skyboxes generated and loaded into Unreal Engine in almost real time.
html:
What if you could change the world you are playing in just by describing it? Say "a lush stylised forest", "an aquarium at the bottom of the ocean with lots of coral and goldfish" or "a city street in the middle of London", and a moment later you are standing in it.

This 2023 prototype chained a few technologies together to do that. Speech is turned into a text prompt, with text to speech talking back to the player. The prompt goes to AI image generation, built with ComfyUI and Blockade Labs' Skybox, to make a full 360° equirectangular panorama. Unreal Engine picks the finished image up while the game is running and wraps it around the player as a new sky, in almost real time.

A scrappy phone recording of the editor, but a glimpse of worlds that build themselves around what you say.

title: Mixed Reality Heritage
blurb: Producing & developing a mixed reality project bringing the past to life at a UNESCO World Heritage building
html:
Watch the video ↗

As part of my research at Liverpool University’s Centre of Architecture and the Visual Arts (CAVA) and in collaboration with Culture Liverpool, Liverpool Institute of Performing Arts, Draw & Code, Immersive Storylab, Cinetecture and Dimension Studios I designed, developed and produced a ground-breaking participatory and immersive mixed reality experience called “If These Walls Could Talk”.

Bringing together world-leading researchers with BAFTA winning writers, a world-class performing arts organisation and immersive technology experts, the team have created a pioneering hybrid spatial experience that considers how audiences can be a part of storytelling.

The location-based prototype was produced for one of Liverpool’s most iconic heritage buildings – the 19th century St George’s Hall (Harvey Lonsdale Elmes, built 1841–1854), which is an intrinsic part of Liverpool’s UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The experience follows the famous court case of Florence Maybrick, who was accused of poisoning her husband, and takes you on a journey back in time to experience and feel what it was like to encounter Liverpool’s late Victorian prison and justice system. Set across the cells and the courtroom at St George’s Hall, the experience uses a variety of technologies such as Virtual Reality, 3d Projection Mapping, Mixed Reality (Microsoft Hololens) and live performance to invite the audience into the last moments of the court case.

The experience used a headset device called the Hololens, which enables users to see both the real world and the virtual one at the same time. With the support of Microsoft’s Mixed Reality team in the US, the team also created the world’s first volumetrically filmed (3D holograms) UNESCO heritage experience using Microsoft’s Mixed Reality capture system at Dimension Studios in London.

Commenting on the experience Peter Woodbridge, the creator and producer of the experience said….”We think the future of heritage experiences is about how you involve an audience as a participant, rather than as a spectator, in the story. This experience combines the real space with virtual objects to enable us to bring the building to life with virtual characters and sound. In this experience the audience is part of the story, also on trial as they encounter holograms, spatial sounds and stories from the past.”

“Our experience takes place across 5,000 square feet of this magnificent UNESCO world heritage building, which was a real challenge in the ways we had to push the technology.”

BAFTA award winning writer Rosemary Kay, Director at Immersive Storylab, and the dialogue writer for the experience says “This allows the audience to feel immersed in the experience of being a prisoner in this grim place, seeing, hearing all the other prisoners around them. The experience treated the audience like Victorian criminals as they were led physically from the dank, cramped cells, past the whipping bench, up the stairs and into the imposing courtroom, where they get tried and found guilty, alongside our historic holograms.”

“We think there’s a real future in these technologies for bringing heritage to life and making us feel a part of the past.”

The team behind the experience have been working on research into spatial storytelling, human performance in mixed reality and augmented reality.

For more info about the project please visit... CAVA

title: Do Objects Dream?
blurb: Producing a Collaboration with National Museums Liverpool's World Cultures Gallery
html:
Re-imagining the display and stories of objects in the World Museum, Liverpool.

Students prototyped and concepted several ways for visitors to be immersively engaged with the stories in this collaboration that led to a new permanent exhibit.

Through the words of T.S. Eliot Prize-winning poet Sarah Howe and an immersive, audio-visual display, our new Chinese ceramics display explores the imagined lives lived by seven objects. This is the first in a series of interventions at the World Cultures gallery in World Museum.

This project was created with the World Museum and ERC-funded TIDE project, along with TIDE visiting poet Sarah Howe, Liverpool John Moores University, Birkenhead School, Meaningful Magic storyboard consultants, Belle Vue Productions, Urban Projections and Adlib installation.

title: Virtual Pop
blurb: Creating a Virtual Pop star to perform at the Royal Television Society awards
html:
I've been helping to bring to life a virtual popstar called Dex with Sum Vivas, working with virtual humans, motion capture, cloth simulation and more to create new possibilities for the metaverse in real-life music events.

So far the digital human avatar, Dex, has been a special guest DJ at the Royal Television Society Awards as part of Classic Decks DJ Set, where she was invited to play alongside human performers & musicians in front of a crowd of over 600 people.

She has also performed at the Bridgewater Hall in Manchester.

title: OctoBot
seoTitle: OctoBot: A Local AI Idea Machine
blurb: A restless pink octopus AI that lives in a folder on your computer and never, ever stops inventing things.
html:
OctoBot is a restless pink octopus AI that lives in a folder on your computer and never, ever stops inventing things: products, gadgets, apps, services, wild experiments and solutions to problems you didn't know you had. Leave it running overnight and wake up to hundreds of idea pitches, each one named, described and saved as its own file.

Under the pixel art it is a fully autonomous agent running a local model through Ollama, so nothing leaves your machine. It picks an idea domain, invents something, saves it to its vault, then fuses past ideas into strange hybrids and follows chains of thought further and wilder. You can chat to it (it drops everything for you), feed it inspiration by dropping files into a folder, or leave it notes, which it answers in its inventor's journal.

A Tamagotchi for ideas, with eight arms and absolutely zero shame. Not serious, but a fun way to play with how autonomous agents loop, remember and build on their own work.

title: EchoLoop
seoTitle: EchoLoop: A Real-Time AI Meeting Copilot
blurb: A real-time AI meeting copilot that listens, transcribes and whispers short, tactical advice every few seconds.
html:
EchoLoop is a real-time AI meeting copilot. It sits quietly on top of your Zoom, Teams or Google Meet window, transcribes what everyone is saying as they say it, and every half a minute or so passes the live transcript to an LLM acting as a personal coach, which comes back with short, tactical nudges: "They sound hesitant on the budget, press now." "Ask for clarification on the timeline." "Pivot to the closing pitch."

Under the hood it captures your microphone and the system audio separately, so it knows who said what, transcribes locally with faster-whisper or in the cloud with Deepgram, and coaches with Claude or GPT. Audio capture, transcription, the LLM and the always-on-top overlay all run in parallel so nothing blocks, with silence detection to skip dead air, a nudge button for advice right now, and a transcript and insight log saved at the end of the session.

Handy for a high-stakes negotiation, or for the fourth back-to-back call of the day, when your brain checked out two meetings ago.

title: Dreamlab Podcaster
seoTitle: Dreamlab Podcaster: Text to Two-Host Podcast
blurb: Turn any newsletter or essay into a natural two-host podcast, with Claude writing the script and ElevenLabs voicing it.
html:
Paste in a newsletter, an essay or anything else, and get back a two-host podcast. Dreamlab Podcaster is a small open-source tool that does the whole job: Claude researches the topics on the web and writes a conversational script, and ElevenLabs turns it into natural, expressive audio.

The show it makes is called Dream Machine, about AI in the creative industries, with two hosts: Elizabeth, who leads with the technical depth, and Pete, who asks the questions the audience would. Claude writes ElevenLabs v3 expression tags straight into the script, like [laughs], [thoughtful] and [pauses], so the voices chuckle, sigh and think rather than just read.

It is built for review rather than blind generation. You can generate the script on its own, edit it, check a 20-second test clip and only then render the full episode, which keeps the cost of each iteration down. It runs as a command-line tool or a Flask web app.

title: Secret Coast
blurb: Producing and developing augmented reality storytelling on the beach.
html:
“It’s hard not to fall in love with Secret Coast” – Digital Catapult, 2018

During early 2018, I worked on an R&D project with a number of partners, supported through the Creative XR content innovation programme from the Digital Catapult and Arts Council England, about an augmented reality experience with coastal communities around the UK.

Britain’s coastline: 11,072 miles of cliffs, beaches, rocky coves, seaside promenades, and towns and villages; it’s a long, winding path with a vibrant history, capturing our powerful social and cultural connection with the sea. The coast of Britain is part of who we are, and very much a place of national contemplation, reflection and emotion.

Coastal communities are saturated with evocative folklore. With stories of tunnel networks, sea caves, piracy, wrecking, slavery, smuggling and mythological creatures and characters. It’s a liminal space not fully explored.

This project set out to explore that and create an interactive location based experience that evokes emotions about this hidden heritage and its connection to our past, present and future.

Using augmented reality’s capabilities at revealing new story worlds, unearthing hidden secrets and bringing invisible culture to life to enable us to re-encounter the landscape through a new kind of reality. Melding together fact and fiction, time and space, past and present the story takes you back to 1790 where the past needs your help to save the future of sealife.

The project includes many features such as complex spatialised AR Scenes, volumetrically filmed content, CGI, mini games, spatial audio, video and interactive content.

title: Beacons for Science

html:
Over the past few months I have been collaborating with a number of partners on the ‘Beacons for Science’ project in Manchester, which is aiming to create an innovative app to experience Science in the City through Augmented and Virtual reality. Using beacon technology to enable people to experience science in new ways as they navigate the city.

My role was to develop the virtual reality and augmented story content, produced with the support of a number of cultural partners, artists, scientists and co-creators from around Manchester, and to work with the developers to shape the mixed reality user-experience.

There are a number of cool features in the app, including virtual reality experiences that are triggered when walking around Manchester as well as interactive augmented reality content that we created to enable people to look behind walls.

There are about 15 experiences in total that were created as a result of a series of hack labs taking place in Manchester as part of the European City of Science calendar.

These include:

  • a Virtual Reality look at the Urban Bees that live on top of Manchester Art Gallery
  • augmented experiences in a number of the libraries around Manchester including Science Footage from the North West Film Archive and the Portico Library
  • a 360 degree performance about the life of Alan Turing
  • a 360 view from the top of the Hilton Hotel
  • an augmented reality experience on the Manchester #astrotram
  • a virtual reality film of the radio telescope at the Jodrell Bank Observatory
  • an augmented reality experiment inspired by John Dalton
  • a Brian Cox ‘Coxemon’ avatar hidden around Manchester
  • a tour of the Manchester Ship Canal
  • #astrotrams – where people can see augmented reality content of the galaxy on a tram that also includes announcements from Professor Brian Cox
  • a virtual statue of RSPB Founder Emily Williamson.

We have also been involved in a series of public engagement events to showcase the Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality content across Manchester during the Euroscience Open Forum 2016 Conference, that has brought over 4000 scientists to the city.

title: Virtual World Museum
blurb: Supporting the iconic World Museum to get online and connect with its audience during its closure.
html:
The experimental technologies lab has been helping the World Museum in Liverpool to rise to the stay-at-home challenge by helping to create a virtual tour of one of the city’s museums.

The World Museum, part of National Museums Liverpool, closed last week in line with government recommendations in a bid to contain the spread of COVID-19 (Coronavirus).

Now, thanks to staff and students at Liverpool John Moores University (including Mark Wright, Peter Horricks and MA Immersive Arts students), the dozens of fascinating exhibits in the World Cultures gallery can be viewed from home by going to a link on the website.

“Staying at home doesn't mean you miss out on visiting our museum,” said Emma Martin, senior curator at National Museums Liverpool.

“We have had a lot of public feedback on what people would like to see while our doors are closed, and have created a virtual tour of the World Cultures gallery with our friends from John Moores.”

With schools and universities closed, children and young people can catch up on history, natural science and anthropology by exploring the extensive collections from Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas.

All you have to do is go to the website at www.liverpoolmuseums.org.uk, click on world cultures virtual gallery tour and navigate your way around the gallery just as you would with apps such as Google Earth.

Pete Woodbridge, course leader on the MA Immersive Arts at LJMU said: “Students have been working with the World Museum this semester to create wonderful new ways for the museum to interact with people via technology.

“These are trying times for everyone, not least parents with children at home, so we are happy to help overcome some of the access issues and keep the museum ‘virtually’ open!”

Focusing on the town centre of Huyton, and working alongside key teams in KMBC (Culture, IT, Development and Communities Team), the project will research and develop creative interventions that put technology at the heart of regeneration and placemaking. It will explore and test the use of the creative applications of interactive media and immersive technologies (AR, Mixed Reality, Sensor-based Media) with the aim of enhancing place and community through innovative approaches to the use of emerging platforms.

Many of the UK's high streets are in a similar situation to Huyton, needing to urgently address new approaches to creating community and experiences that will encourage significant improvements in footfall, community building and economic activity.

title: Immersive Symposium
blurb: Producing a research symposium about XR Content Design and Development
html:
“Immersive experiences require novel narrative mechanisms & new language of production… The best technology will not produce the change needed without equal excellence in content production and understanding of immersion as a narrative form” – Creative Industries Review 2017

On December 14th 2018, Liverpool Screen School welcomed over 200 guests from industry and academia, with 8 panels, and over 30 speakers and demos, to discuss the way that Immersive Technologies such as AR, VR, MR, XR and AI are impacting on storytelling.

The day included panels exploring the diverse ways in which people are engaging with new technologies. Speakers included creative writers, theatremakers, game developers, filmmakers, artists, creative coders and academics discussing how they are approaching the emerging mediums of virtual reality, augmented reality, digital theatre, projection mapping and mixed reality for storytelling experiences. The talks addressed creative research & development into defining languages of production, narrative mechanisms and approaches to engaging audiences in experiential media across the spectrum of immersive technology.

Speakers included thinkers and creative talent from BBC R&D, Digital Catapult’s CreativeXR Programme, Bristol VR Lab, XR Stories from York, Institute of Creative Technologies in Leicester, Liverpool Screen School and practice-based academics from a number of Universities from across the UK.

Companies included Marshmallow Laser Feast, Draw and Code, Limbik Theatre, Pilot Theatre, Boom Clap Play, Kinicho, Production Park, The Hatch, Mnemoscene, Immersive Storylab and Charisma.ai. There were also a number of demos including a 6 metre immersive dome from Igloo Vision and a Magic Leap, a new Sonic Reality engine by Kinicho and a preview of Robert Eagle's amazing Through the Wardrobe work.

Liverpool Screen School’s own work on using immersive storytelling for climate change activism and their use of mixed reality and augmented reality to create novel storytelling experiences was also on show. The day also included work from the AHRC’s Immersive Experiences programme including projects that enable people to experience a forgotten castle in Sheffield and a digital ghost hunt project in London.

There were also many other projects on display that give a glimpse into the possibilities, including a project to bring augmented reality to trains across the UK, a project that used mixed reality to reconnect Somali communities with heritage, dance and performance projects that blend digital and physical space, and talks about the way that programmers are working with oral storytelling traditions. The event also explored how digital place is affecting physical communities and there were also projects that were using storytelling to tackle health issues and even to question gender norms. People talked about MoCAP, Volumetric Video and new tools for creating more realistic environments and interactions in virtual worlds.

Pete Woodbridge, Event Producer and Co-Director of the Experimental Technologies Lab, said,

“Storytelling is certainly going through a renaissance and it’s amazing how this technology is bringing so many creative disciplines together. We had such a range of thinking and approaches being discussed on the day and it's a really great time to be working in such a collaborative area of research and practice.

"There’s real desire to move storytelling beyond the limitations of the screen and put people inside experiences, or to paraphrase Robin McNicholas from Marshmallow Laser Feast ‘it’s about taking things out of the rectangle and into the real world’."

Exciting times.

Thanks to LJMU and the brilliant Rachel McClean, Jane Leah, Jayne Bryson, Chris Chadwick and Mark Smith for helping to make this all happen.

title: Story Scopes
blurb: Creating an Augmented Reality Storytelling Telescope Experience
html:
StoryScopes are public viewing telescopes that I developed that tell stories using augmented reality and sound. The device enables people to see stories in landscapes and bring environments to life with history and future visualisations.

From seeing history and imagination unfold before your eyes in mountains and the oceans, to visualising urban development and enhancing landmarks, the storyscopes device is aiming to get people to learn more about their surroundings by combining the digital and physical world.

Using head tracking and games based interactions, users can also interact with the digital and physical content they see using the device, from playing games across cityscapes to engaging in interactive narratives. There’s also the ability to teleport into virtual worlds and see beyond the immediate environment.

Installation options include single devices and multiple scopes to encourage exploration through stories, mysteries and interactivity.

We used storyscopes to test out a few ideas around getting storytelling in place, including working with AND Festival in 2021, doing technical consulting with McCann Manchester, to support an artist developing a similar project on the Mersey Ferry.

We also have screen based (holographic) viewing options to enable a number of ways for groups to share the experience. There is also the option for the device to take micro-payments for revenue generation.

title: Shaun in Shanghai

The aim of this research/industry partnership is to collaborate on a unique, location-based, mixed reality immersive experience in a specially designed theatre in Shanghai.

"Shaun the Sheep" is already a global entertainment brand known principally for its linear, animated, non-dialogue content (movies; TV series). This project will therefore focus on technical, creative and business innovation rather than on audience acquisition. It will also put Aardman at the forefront of developing innovation, new methods, new knowledge and, through creating new audiences, access to a new market.

In terms of technological innovation, the team will seek a collaboration with partners in the UK and China. By using mixed reality technology (e.g. holograms tracked by computer vision), the project envisions to blur the traditional boundaries between the screen, theatre and cinema space, creating a new "narrative space" in which audiences are part of and feel fully immersed.

title: MA Immersive Arts
blurb: Developing a postgraduate course in Immersive Experiences, Mixed Reality / XR Creative Practice
html:
I've been developing a new MA Course between Liverpool Screen School and Liverpool School of Art and Design.

The MA in Immersive Arts explores immersive storytelling experiences, augmented reality, projection mapping, interactive environments, holographics and mixed reality content production and experience design.

The MA Immersive Arts is a pioneering degree where students will explore and experiment with making applications, prototypes and experiences in augmented reality, mixed reality, projection mapping, holographics, future screens and virtual reality. It is run collaboratively between the Liverpool Screen School and the Liverpool School of Art and Design in dedicated lab facilities, with access to cutting-edge equipment, software and practical research expertise.

From design, education, marketing and health to entertainment, arts and theatre, immersive technologies have been making an impact across a number of sectors over the last few years. This course will prepare students with the skills and conceptual abilities to develop content, experiences and applications for a number of industries.

Exploring techniques and innovation in immersive storytelling, experience design, content creation, artistic practice, exhibition and installation. This course will enable students to develop the next generation of spatial experiences in an industry that is predicted to have a huge growth over the next decade.

Modules include:

  • Immersive Storytelling - where students will learn about the techniques used to engage audiences in immersive experiences across a variety of platforms and contexts. Drawing upon areas such as experience design, games design, immersive theatre, interactive media and immersive arts practice.
  • Immersive Arts Lab - learning practical creative skills across experience design in mixed reality, augmented reality, binaural sound, volumetric and spatial design, interactive development, sensor based media and immersive display techniques.
  • Collaborative Project - working collaboratively with peers and an external partner, responding to an arts, media and design challenge and/or an opportunity for working on socially engaged immersive practice.
  • Research and Proposal - developing R&D skills and knowledge to develop, test and prototype a creative practice proposal.
  • Immersive Arts Project - A major practice-based creative project in an area of interest to you.

It expands on the University's internationally recognised research and teaching from media, film, art and design- which includes research across immersive arts, immersive documentary and fiction production, 3d digital art, augmented reality, mixed reality, holographics, virtual reality and immersive theatre. The team behind it has recently put on the Immersive Storytelling Research Symposium involving industry and academics from across the UK to explore the future of research in these growing mediums.

It is aimed at creatives with diverse backgrounds in digital art & design, media & film, animation and 3d modelling, motion graphics, computer science & games, theatre and music production. This interdisciplinary course is designed to appeal to people looking at developing and shaping their immersive practice and creative skills.

Peter Woodbridge, Programme Leader, says “It’s a really exciting time to be working at the intersection of creativity, storytelling, digital arts and emerging technology. We wanted to design a course that wasn't just focused on virtual reality headsets, although we cover that too, and we are incorporating a wide range of practical immersive technology skills into the programme. This includes spatial experience design, projection mapping, augmented reality, binaural sound, physical-digital art practice and new capture, simulation and display techniques and technologies."

"Students on this course will be investigating and inventing new ways to engage audiences in spatial story and arts experiences by learning about what happens when our definitions of media arts go beyond the screen. It’s about making new possibilities, ideas, experiences, installations and applications for engaging audiences across a number of areas.”

The course is being developed in consultation with creative industry, arts and wider business partners, including a number of national companies and organisations, as well as Liverpool's and the North West's thriving immersive technology sector.

seoTitle: ShadowText: Words That Fill Your Shadow
blurb: A webcam piece where light carves the body from darkness and words pour into the shadow around you.
html:
Where light carves the body from darkness, and words fill the space between.

ShadowText turns your webcam into a living canvas. Text lives in the negative: it flows into every corner the light leaves behind, wrapping your silhouette, tracing the edges of absence and flooding the shadow with language. Words drift, pulse and spring as you move.

It runs entirely in the browser, with MediaPipe face and body segmentation to find the shape of you and the Pretext layout engine to pour the text around it. The words can be your own, live RSS headlines, song lyrics, or written on the fly by a local model running in LM Studio. No server, no upload: the camera never leaves the room.

title: Maritime AR
blurb: Augmented Reality Storytelling & System design for Boats
html:
Our seas tell many tales.

Imagine taking a ferry or cruise and seeing the past coming alive around you: viking battles in the Irish Sea, a shark circling the boat, Odysseus fighting a sea monster, the Titanic hitting an iceberg, a giant statue appearing from a long lost civilisation, a ghost ship slowly gliding past you, a WWII battle in the skies. Imagine being able to find out and connect to the stories of famous landmarks as you drift by port as you participate in augmented games, stories and shared adventures that help you pass the time and connect you to the journey and the people around you. Not only would this provide a wonderfully unexpected diversion on the journey but also a way to highlight landmarks that often go unnoticed by passengers as they come in to land, representing a new opportunity to connect passengers to media content and advertising.

Maritime AR: The Odyssey was a 3 month design foundations industrial research project that I led between Immersive StoryLab, Meyouandus, LJMU and Maritime Industry stakeholders. It resulted in the development of several reports and new design/prototype for putting Augmented Reality systems in the sea, with a platform aimed at passengers on cruise ships and boats.

The location triggered content can be viewed in a number of ways, through mobile devices, on board portholes and special customised viewers that connect people to the stories and the facts about their surroundings.

The work will be presented to an international audience of boat designers and researchers at the International Marine Design Conference, Cadiz, Spain 2020

title: Theatre in a Box
blurb: Making Theatre work small with Holographic Displays
html:
Hey little people…..

Going to the theatre is a big deal.

You have to buy big tickets for big bucks, get dressed in your big clothes, then get on a big grown up train, then queue up for big drinks, then speak to big people….

and that’s before you have to deal with watching all the big egos, the big set ups and all the big massive convoluted drama.

It puts you off right?

That’s because being big is a pain. Most people appreciate the little things in life. Well we’ve just invented the perfect thing for you.

It’s just a little box, that sits on your table or your kitchen counter, allowing you to experience a little bit of drama, in a little place, that’s convenient for you.

Welcome to Theatre in a Box (TM).

It’s a little revolution. It’s the future. It’s massive (in a little kind of way), especially if you are an ant.

The project is hoping to raise money to restore a really important community asset to communicate its potential as a space.

title: StoryHack
blurb: Producing An Immersive Residency in Liverpool
html:
STORYHACK was a 4 day educational residency designed to give creatives the knowledge, skills and tools to begin to use new technologies and interactivity in their work in a fundamental and transformative way.

This intensive course is led by immersive artists Simon Wilkinson (Circa69) and Myra Appannah (dotdot). It aims to help artists move beyond disciplines, adopt new creative and design approaches and to capture new audiences and expectations.

It is designed as a reboot for those currently working in non-interactive mediums, who want to reboot their practice, to work across a combination of platforms and create culture which gives audiences a meaningful role in adaptive works.

The course covered approaches to design, collaboration, production and immersive technologies including; Unity Games Engine, virtual reality, augmented reality, games system design, speculative design, interaction design, 3D modelling, visual scripting tools, dealing with complexity in interactive narratives, transmedia storytelling, photogrammetry and liquid studio approaches to collaboration.

It was hosted by the Experimental Technologies Lab, in the Institute for Art and Technology, at Liverpool School of Art and Design as part of the development of the new MA in Immersive Arts.

title: Lumiere 3D
blurb: Bringing Lumiere's moving image work into another dimension
html:
Our team worked with perceptual psychologist Rob Black, from a company called Realspace, to develop a unique new way of viewing a piece of cinematic history.

In 1897 the pioneering Lumiere brothers famously filmed the world’s first tracking shot to capture the magic of the world’s first electric overhead railway – the Liverpool Overhead Railway (LOR). The shot is a continuous record of the expansive Liverpool docks and is a hugely significant part of the heritage of industry in the UK.

The team created a new way to watch the footage, using a perceptual psychology trick, to make the film appear in three dimensions, creating a real sense of depth.

We then placed this into a virtual reality headset for an immersive experience with the past.

title: Immersive Health
blurb: An Immersive Liverpool event on immersive technology in health and wellbeing.
description: An Immersive Liverpool event with BIMA, Juice Immersive and Alder Hey Innovation Hub on how VR and AR can change healthcare, clinical training and wellbeing.
html:
From visualising clinical processes and procedures, to experiential training for health practitioners and patient centred interventions, immersive technologies such as virtual reality and augmented reality, have huge potential for disrupting the way we think about healthcare and wellbeing in the future.

This event, in collaboration with BIMA, Immersive Liverpool, Juice Immersive and Alder Hey Innovation Hub will be exploring the wide ranging impacts of immersive technology in the health and clinical sector. Ranging from applications in consumer health, to training environments and surgical innovations. We’ll hear from a range of innovators from around the Liverpool City Region and beyond.

Speakers and Demonstrators

Alder Hey Innovation Hub will talk about their programmes and ways that they can support businesses in developing innovations, products and services for the NHS, clinical and health markets.

Dr Rafael Guerrero, Director of the Heart Unit, Alder Hey Children’s Hospital. A surgeon who is working to develop novel ways that use AR and VR for surgical heart analysis and procedures.

Immersive Interactive are the UK’s leading provider of fully immersive learning spaces in both education and emergency service sectors. They provide virtual learning spaces that are fully interactive and multisensory. Utilising bespoke content, their rooms create unique educational and training experiences that are both effective and memorable. They will have a set up of their Immersive Space—which is a cutting edge learning tool that engages users through sight, sound, smell, and touch.

Paul Duval, University of Liverpool Medical School will showcase and talk about the potential of VR in Medical Education. Paul has recently been working on a project called ‘Virtual Immersive Clinical Simulation (VICS)’ exploring how the experiential benefits of virtual reality can take classroom and simulation based learning to another level in clinical training.

Arjun Panesar, Diabetes.co.uk (Diabetes Digital Media), will be presenting their virtual reality projects exploring relationships with food, for education around Type 1 Diabetes. Current research indicates fluctuating glucose levels in children with diabetes may be associated with corresponding fluctuations in brain volume. The Type 1 Program addresses this by using a reinforcement learning approach to VR gamification to explore relationships with food.

ImmerseUK is a cross-sector network for businesses, research and educational organisations across the UK that are interested in immersive technologies, including augmented, virtual and mixed realities. They will be talking about the work they have been doing in encouraging innovation in immersive technology, as well as the findings of UK wide research project mapping the Immersive Economy.

Innovation @ Alder Hey

Alder Hey Children’s hospital has embarked on an award winning innovation programme. The Hospital’s Innovation Service operates from a 1000m2 Innovation Hub which provides a space for health care professionals, industry and academia to drive the best of new technology into healthcare. Working with key technologies including Artificial Intelligence, Sensors and Virtual Reality, the team helps partners create, develop and test new innovations. Its role as a partner in the ERDF-funded Health Innovation Exchange programme is a key enabler of its work with industry. The programme’s seven partners help Liverpool City Region based technology, creative digital and life science companies to develop and bring new innovation to the health, well-being and social care markets.

The Spark Compass platform™ manages data from user devices, wearables and sensor networks, enabling the delivery of smart content. This is done by analysing data patterns, setting specific rules and combining existing data sources. Powerful analytics on collected performance data, real-time behavior and actions provide granular visibility in a centralised platform.

Using trans-disciplinary design principles developed by Prof Koeck and Dr Kocaturk, the team of researchers, including myself, worked on a research project and report called "intelligent, real-time, hyper-local screen-based OoH marketing" with the aim to innovate new ideas that ultimately could transform interactions between people and urban screens and mobile devices.

"We wanted to find new ways to engage audiences in interactive, immersive technologies, which will allow people who are interested in the architecture of the city to audio-visually perceive the city in unprecedented ways," Professor Koeck said.

The research is part of a broad scope of work at the University which harnesses the digital revolution and also draws upon our heritage to meet the challenges of today.

title: University IT Service Desk Simulator
seoTitle: University IT Simulator: AI Text Game
blurb: An AI-powered text survival game in which you try to complete one simple administrative task at a university. You will fail.
html:
A text-based survival simulator, powered by AI, in which you attempt one simple administrative task at a university: claiming back £4.20 for a train ticket, getting access to the S: drive, or replacing a mouse that keeps giving you electric shocks. You will fail. You will be redirected. You will be transferred to Procurement, who are at lunch.

You play a student, a new employee or a seasoned employee, and an LLM plays the exhausted service desk and every department it passes you on to: Finance, who mention the migration constantly; Estates, who are confused about why IT sent you; HR, with a 47-page PDF and a meeting in six weeks. Three live counters track the damage, time wasted, people involved and policies survived, and the numbers only go up.

You can win, by finding a genuine loophole, escalating with such sustained bureaucratic fury that someone caves, or finding the one human who will whisper how to do it properly. A love letter to everyone who has ever lost a week of their life to a form.

title: StoryVaultOS
blurb: A local-first, multi-agent AI writers' room for screenwriters and story developers, where nothing lands without your approval.
html:
StoryVaultOS is a creative development environment for screenwriters, novelists and showrunners who want AI collaboration on their own terms. It runs on your own machine, keeps everything as plain Markdown files, and gives you a team of 11 specialised AI agents, each with its own voice and job: Writer, Critic, Editor, Archivist, Producer, Character, Structure, Logline, Treatment, Lore and Showrunner.

The key design principle is a human in the loop. No agent writes directly to your story. Every suggestion, revision and new scene is a proposal you review as a diff and then approve or reject. Send a task to the whole team and the agents debate, critique each other and come back with a recommendation, over as many rounds as you choose. A knowledge base tracks characters, locations, creatures and world rules, and every change is checked against your canon, so contradictions get flagged before they creep in.

Built for the long project, the feature, the pilot, the series bible or the novel, where continuity matters and you need a system that remembers everything you have decided. Not a one-click story generator, but a toolkit for serious story development.
